title: Automated Attribution of Unknown Cryptocurrency Wallets to Nearest Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) through Blockchain Intelligence APIs
department: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C),CIS Division
description:
• Background The rapid adoption of Virtual Digital Assets (VDAs) and decentralized blockchain ecosystems has significantly increased the complexity of cybercrime investigations globally. Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs) frequently encounter cryptocurrency wallet addresses linked to cyber frauds, ransomware, investment scams, darknet activities, and laundering of crime proceeds.
Under the existing investigation workflow, LEAs raise lawful information disclosure requests through the SAHYOG Portal to Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) such as crypto exchanges, custodial wallet providers, and trading platforms. However, in many cases, the suspect wallet identified during investigations belongs to an unhosted wallet or a wallet for which the associated VASP is unknown. This creates major delays in attribution, freezing of assets, and identification of the beneficial owner.
Blockchain transactions generally pass through multiple intermediary wallets before reaching centralized exchanges. Identifying the 'nearest direct deposit accepting exchange' manually through blockchain analysis is time-consuming and requires specialized expertise.
• Description The proposed system envisages development of an Automated Blockchain Intelligence & VASP Attribution Engine integrated with the SAHYOG Portal through APIs.
The system should:
• Automatically analyze suspect cryptocurrency wallet addresses reported during investigations on the Sahyog Platform
• Automatically trace blockchain transaction paths to identify:
o nearest centralized exchange, o custodial wallet service, o or VASP receiving direct deposits from the suspect wallet.
• Map blockchain of deposit addresses and transaction flows across multiple blockchain networks such as:
o Bitcoin, o Ethereum, o Tron, o BNB Chain, o Solana, o Polygon o and other major chains.
• Support identification of:
o exchange clusters, o hot wallets, o deposit wallets, o mixers/tumblers, o DeFi bridges, o and cross-chain swap services.
• Integrate Sahyog with blockchain intelligence APIs and graph analytics engines.
• Provide automated tagging and confidence scoring for suspected VASPs.
• Generate investigation-ready reports for LEAs.
• Assist investigators in automatically routing lawful disclosure or freezing requests to the correct VASP through the SAHYOG Portal.
The system may additionally support:
• visualization of fund movement,
• cross-chain transaction mapping,
• risk scoring,
• identification of laundering typologies,
• and alerting for high-risk wallets linked to ransomware, darknet, terrorism financing, or fraud ecosystems.
• Expected Solution A software-based blockchain intelligence platform integrated with the SAHYOG ecosystem capable of:
• Automated identification of nearest VASP/exchange linked to unknown wallets.
• API-driven blockchain tracing and attribution support.
• Multi-chain transaction analysis and visualization.
• Real-time generation of investigative intelligence.
• Risk classification of wallets and transaction flows.
• Dashboard for LEAs with case-based analytics and reporting.
• Scalable architecture capable of handling large-volume blockchain transaction analysis.
The solution should aim to:
• reduce investigation time,
• improve asset freezing efficiency,
• enhance attribution capabilities,
• and strengthen cross-border cybercrime investigations involving VDAs
summary: Innovation (3/5): draws on blockchain applied to a blockchain & cybersecurity problem, placing it in the moderate band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Blockchain & Cybersecurity. Tech Depth (5/5): centers on api, blockchain, real-time. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 20/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Automated Attribution of Unknown Cryptocurrency Wallets to Nearest Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) through Blockchain Intelligence APIs

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a tool that takes a suspicious crypto wallet address reported in a cybercrime case and automatically traces where the money actually went, through however many hop wallets, to find the real exchange or platform that can freeze it, instead of an investigator doing that tracing by hand.
overview.why_it_matters: When investigators find a suspect wallet, it's often not the wallet holding the actual funds, they're layered through intermediary wallets first. Manually tracing that chain to find the exchange that can act on a freeze request is slow and specialized, and every hour lost is an hour the funds have to move further away.
pain_points: Suspect wallets identified during investigations are frequently unhosted or linked to an unknown VASP, stalling the legal process to freeze assets.
Blockchain transactions pass through multiple intermediary wallets before reaching a centralized exchange, and tracing that path manually requires specialized expertise most investigators don't have.
The existing SAHYOG portal disclosure-request workflow assumes you already know which VASP to ask, this PS is about filling that gap.
overview.background: Rapid adoption of virtual digital assets has significantly increased cybercrime investigation complexity. Law enforcement raises disclosure requests to VASPs through the SAHYOG portal, but when the suspect wallet is unhosted or its VASP is unknown, this creates major delays in attribution, asset freezing, and identifying the beneficial owner. Manual blockchain tracing to find the nearest deposit-accepting exchange is time-consuming and requires specialized skill.
overview.whats_being_asked: An Automated Blockchain Intelligence & VASP Attribution Engine integrated with the SAHYOG Portal via APIs, that ingests reported wallet addresses, automatically performs blockchain tracing to identify the nearest exchange or VASP receiving direct deposits, detects fund-movement patterns, and generates actionable intelligence for investigators.
expected_solution: Ingestion of victim/investigator-reported wallet addresses through the cybercrime complaint workflow.
Automated blockchain transaction-graph tracing to identify the nearest centralized exchange or VASP receiving direct deposits.
Detection of exchange-wallet clusters, hot wallets, deposit wallets, mixers/tumblers, DeFi bridges, and cross-chain swap services.
Support for multiple blockchain ecosystems (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, BNB Chain, Solana, Polygon, and others).
Integration with SAHYOG/NCRP platforms, automated alert generation, and risk categorization of wallets, with an analytics dashboard for investigators.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate band. Blockchain transaction tracing and exchange-cluster identification are established techniques used by real commercial blockchain-forensics firms, the innovation for a hackathon team is building a workable, focused version of that pipeline using available public blockchain-intelligence APIs, not inventing new tracing algorithms.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Multi-chain transaction-graph tracing, cluster/mixer detection, and a SAHYOG-style integration and dashboard together represent genuine breadth, even scoped to one or two blockchains.

competitive_landscape.note: Crypto-fraud tracing is a recurring SIH theme from I4C, and this specific PS overlaps significantly with SIH26183 (same organization, adjacent framing), teams should read both PS carefully and differentiate their submission clearly if considering either.

innovation.note: Blockchain forensics/clustering is an established field, the value here is a working, focused hackathon-scale implementation, not a novel technique.

invention.note: Multi-chain tracing, cluster detection, and platform integration together represent real engineering breadth, best tackled by scoping to one blockchain (Bitcoin or Ethereum) for the working demo.

technical_feasibility.note: Real blockchain intelligence APIs (Chainalysis-style tools) are largely commercial/paywalled, plan around free-tier or open blockchain-explorer APIs (Etherscan, Blockchain.info) and be upfront about that limitation.

impact_and_benefits.note: Faster VASP attribution has a direct, well-articulated law-enforcement benefit: faster asset freezing and higher fund-recovery odds for victims.

architecture.note: A graph-tracing engine feeding a clustering/detection layer and a dashboard is a clean, well-understood architecture pattern, manageable in 36 hours if scoped to one blockchain.

overall_verdict.reasoning: A credible pick for a team comfortable with blockchain data structures, scoped to one chain (Bitcoin or Ethereum, both have strong free/public block-explorer APIs) with a genuinely working transaction-graph trace, rather than claiming multi-chain support that isn't actually implemented and tested.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Public block-explorer APIs (Etherscan, Blockchain.info, and similar) provide genuinely real, live transaction data to trace against, this doesn't need to be faked or simulated the way many other PS in this batch require.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Claiming support for six blockchain ecosystems when only one is actually implemented and tested is an easy overclaim that a technically sharp judge will probe and expose quickly, scope honestly.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Confirm hour 0: which blockchain will be your fully-working demo chain (recommend Ethereum or Bitcoin for the best free API/tooling support), and have you tested at least one real transaction trace against it before committing the architecture?

idea_0_4: Pick one blockchain to fully implement (Ethereum is a strong choice: Etherscan API is free, well-documented, and widely used).
Get a basic transaction-graph trace working against a real, known wallet address immediately, this validates your core technical approach before building anything else on top.
Assign owners: one on the tracing/graph engine, one on the clustering/mixer-detection logic, one on the investigator-facing dashboard and SAHYOG-style workflow mockup.
prototype_4_22: Build the transaction-graph tracer: given a wallet address, walk forward through transactions to find deposit destinations, using real API data.
Build basic exchange-wallet identification, known exchange hot-wallet address lists are publicly available and are a fast, honest way to identify 'nearest known VASP'.
In parallel, build the investigator dashboard shell showing case intake and trace-in-progress status.
integration_22_30: Wire the full pipeline: wallet address input -> automated trace -> identified exchange/VASP (or flagged as unresolved) -> risk categorization output.
Add basic mixer/intermediary-wallet flagging (wallets with unusually high fan-in/fan-out patterns are a reasonable heuristic).
Test against several real, publicly-known fraud-linked wallet addresses (many are documented in public blockchain-forensics writeups) to validate your trace actually reaches a plausible exchange.
polish_30_36: Prepare a live demo: input a real wallet address, watch the system trace it through the blockchain graph to an identified exchange, live.
Prepare an honest scope statement: which blockchain(s) are fully implemented versus described as an extension.
Build a clean visualization of the transaction graph, this is inherently visual and will land well with judges.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Trace a real, publicly documented fraud-linked wallet address live during the demo (several are publicly known from past incidents and blockchain-forensics writeups) rather than a synthetic example, this proves your tracing engine works against genuine, messy real-world blockchain data.

strengths: Real, free blockchain data APIs mean the core demo can be built and tested against genuine data, not simulation.
Transaction-graph visualization is inherently compelling and easy for judges to follow visually.
weaknesses: Significant overlap with the adjacent SIH26183 PS risks confused positioning if a team doesn't differentiate clearly.
Full commercial-grade blockchain intelligence (mixer detection, cross-chain tracing) is genuinely hard, easy to overclaim capability that wasn't actually built.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: 2 blockchain/backend-focused to 1 frontend, the tracing and clustering logic is the technical core and credibility anchor.
team_fit.approach: Validate real API access and a real transaction trace in the first hour, before designing anything else, if the chosen blockchain API has rate limits or access issues, you need to know that immediately, not at hour 20.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Block-explorer API integration boilerplate, graph-traversal logic, and dashboard scaffolding can be built quickly with AI coding assistance.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Deciding what heuristics genuinely indicate mixer/laundering behavior (versus legitimate high-volume wallet activity) needs domain research and careful validation, false positives here have real investigative consequences.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-generated 'multi-chain, mixer-detecting, exchange-clustering' pipeline that was only ever tested on one synthetic example and never against real transaction data will fall apart the moment a judge asks to see it trace a real wallet.

data_resource_availability.status: Free-tier public block-explorer APIs exist for major chains (Etherscan for Ethereum, Blockchain.info for Bitcoin), full commercial blockchain-intelligence tools (Chainalysis, Elliptic) are paywalled and out of reach for a hackathon build.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If API rate limits become a problem during the hackathon, pre-fetch and cache transaction data for your demo wallet addresses ahead of time, and be transparent that the live demo uses cached data standing in for a live-query architecture.

judge_qna.question: How does this compare to commercial tools like Chainalysis that law enforcement already uses?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We're not claiming to replace commercial-grade tooling, we built a focused, working proof-of-concept on one blockchain using free public APIs, showing the core attribution logic works, real deployment would integrate with licensed commercial intelligence feeds for full coverage.
judge_qna.follow_up: What specifically would need to change to make this production-ready alongside a tool like Chainalysis?

judge_qna.question: How do you avoid false positives when flagging a wallet as a mixer or laundering intermediary?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We used [specific heuristic, e.g. fan-in/fan-out ratio and transaction timing patterns], validated against known mixer addresses, and we flag with a confidence score rather than a binary yes/no, since we know it's an imperfect heuristic.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your false-positive rate against a set of known legitimate high-volume wallets?

judge_qna.question: This PS looks very similar to another one in the batch (SIH26183), how is your build different?
judge_qna.strong_answer: We focused specifically on the automated SAHYOG-integrated attribution workflow for investigator-initiated tracing, [explain your specific differentiation, e.g. deeper multi-chain support or the risk-categorization layer].
judge_qna.follow_up: If you had to pick one, which of the two PS does your actual build better satisfy, and why?
